brief.headline: Samsung-Hynix divergence sharpens as HBM4 ramp meets DRAM pricing supercycle; CoWoS easing 2H26
brief.summary: <cite index="1-1,1-2">SK Hynix completed world-first HBM4 development in September 2025 with mass production ready, delivering doubled bandwidth and 40% better power efficiency versus HBM3E</cite>. <cite index="3-2,3-3,3-5">Samsung cleared Production Readiness Approval for HBM4 and shipped samples to Nvidia exceeding 11 Gbps requirements for Rubin platform</cite>. <cite index="10-6,10-7">Spot DRAM pricing surged with DDR4 8Gb at $24 in July (+14.3% MoM), while NAND hit $30.1 (+4.3% MoM), both setting record highs on 19-month consecutive gains</cite>. <cite index="17-2,17-6">Hyperscaler capex accelerated to $660-690B in 2026, nearly doubling 2025 levels, with all providers reporting supply-constrained rather than demand-constrained markets</cite>. <cite index="28-1,28-7">TSMC's CoWoS supply-demand gap is narrowing from 20% currently to 10% by end-2026 as monthly capacity reaches 120-140k wafers</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="37-2,37-3">Samsung offers exposure to conventional DRAM pricing strength, improving HBM competitiveness and larger shareholder returns, while SK Hynix remains the purer bet on premium HBM and Nvidia-led AI infrastructure cycle</cite>. <cite index="37-8">Samsung reclaimed DRAM revenue leadership at 39% share versus SK Hynix 26%</cite>, reducing HBM dependency as commodity pricing inflects. <cite index="4-1">HBM3E will remain dominant in 2026 at two-thirds of total HBM shipments even as HBM4 ramps</cite>, favoring Hynix's entrenched position. <cite index="5-3,5-4">Samsung plans ~47% HBM capacity increase to 250k wafers/month by end-2026 from current 170k, roughly matching Hynix but output has lagged due to Nvidia qualification challenges</cite>. Relative call: neutral near-term, tilt Samsung on broadening DRAM upcycle and capital return optionality, but Hynix retains HBM pricing power through 1H27.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="13-2,13-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 58-63% QoQ in Q2 2026, NAND jumped 70-75% QoQ, following Q1's record 90-95% DRAM increase</cite>. <cite index="14-5,14-6">Memory makers plan to reduce PC DRAM supply as cloud providers increase server memory purchases; TrendForce forecasts PC DRAM prices rising 15-20% in Q3</cite>. <cite index="9-9,9-10">AI inference and hyperscale demand keeps supply constrained as manufacturers shift capacity toward higher-margin server products, leaving less for consumer memory</cite>. <cite index="13-10,13-12">Meaningful capacity expansion not expected until late 2027 at earliest; cloud providers willing to pay more and commit to multi-quarter purchase agreements</cite>. Consumer affordability limits emerging but enterprise pricing remains uncapped through 2027.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="2-2,2-4">HBM3E supply remains tight and lags demand as Samsung and SK Hynix prioritize ramping HBM4; mainstream HBM3E prices expected to ease as HBM4 enters market but ongoing AI accelerator launches keep demand on steady growth path</cite>. <cite index="2-5,2-7">H200 export approval to China exceeded expectations with each chip incorporating six HBM3E stacks; analysts forecast 2026 HBM revenue mix at ~55% HBM4 and 45% HBM3E, with HBM4 beginning Q3 to rapidly absorb prior HBM3E demand</cite>. <cite index="5-1">Both Samsung and SK Hynix started delivering paid final HBM4 samples to Nvidia</cite>. <cite index="5-7,5-8">SK Hynix will start commercial 1b DRAM production for HBM4 at M15X fab in February, four months ahead of schedule, initially at ~10k wafers/month scaling severalfold by end-2026</cite>. <cite index="3-4">HBM4 expected to deliver roughly 60% higher bandwidth than current HBM3E</cite>. Qualification risk tilts Hynix near-term but Samsung closing gap for 2H26 Rubin ramp.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix completes world-first HBM4 development, ready for mass production
news_pulse.implication: Hynix maintains first-mover advantage in next-gen HBM; 2x bandwidth, 40% power efficiency gain sustains pricing power into Rubin cycle. Samsung 3-6 month lag risk.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix plan ~20% HBM3E price hike for 2026 as Nvidia H200, ASIC demand rises
news_pulse.implication: HBM3E pricing inflection despite HBM4 launch; H200 China approval adding incremental demand. Extends margin tailwind through 1H26 even as HBM4 ramps.

news_pulse.headline: July DRAM, NAND prices hit record highs again on AI demand
news_pulse.implication: DDR4 8Gb at $24 (+14.3% MoM), 8x increase since June 2016 survey start. Conventional DRAM pricing now contributing meaningfully to Samsung/Hynix revenue mix; reduces HBM dependency.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance reaches $660-690B, up 81% YoY
news_pulse.implication: Amazon $200B, Alphabet $175-185B, Meta $115-135B, Microsoft $120B+, Oracle $50B. All report supply-constrained not demand-constrained. Secures HBM/DRAM demand visibility through 2027.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from 20% to 10% by end-2026
news_pulse.implication: Monthly CoWoS capacity reaching 120-140k wafers in 2026. Easing packaging bottleneck de-risks HBM supply chain, reduces hyperscaler allocation friction 2H26.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC begins large-scale outsourcing of critical CoW process to ASE, others
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia reserved 800-850k CoWoS wafers for 2026 (>50% of TSMC capacity). CoW outsourcing marks major supply chain shift; increases elasticity, reduces single-point risk for AI chip production.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung plans 50% HBM capacity surge in 2026, spotlight on HBM4
news_pulse.implication: Target 250k wafers/month by end-2026 vs current 170k. Investment centered on HBM4; converting existing lines and expanding P4. Narrows capacity gap with Hynix but qualification timeline key.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung stock rebounds, SK Hynix sinks: Korea AI trade diverging today
news_pulse.implication: Samsung reclaiming DRAM revenue leadership (39% vs Hynix 26%) reduces HBM dependency. Broad earnings engine benefits from conventional DRAM upcycle; capital return potential lifts valuation multiple.
